Requirements include an Apple home hub, an iCloud+ subscription, a motion sensor, and setting up the camera as a standalone HomeKit accessory. Recording must be enabled separately for each camera. items.title: [Fast Company] A popular password manager was hacked. Here’s what you need to know
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Password managers are the safest way short of secret sticky notes to keep track of the hundreds of logins in your life, but even they don’t have perfect security.

Popular Password manager 1Password disclosed this week that hackers breached its systems this month and accessed the software’s source code. While no breach is good news, the attackers were not able to access 1Password users’ most sensitive data, including their passwords, secret keys, and information stored in user vaults. 

“At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the company emphasized in a blog post on the incident. The security of the software maker’s apps and browser extensions was also not affected by the breach.

The attackers were able to burrow into 1Password’s system after gaining access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. By pushing malicious code into its backend systems, the attackers made off with administrative data on a subset of 1Password customers, including customer names, email addresses, and “non-secret internal metadata” about accounts. 

Anyone who uses 1Password doesn’t need to take extra steps right now, but they should be extra vigilant for phishing attempts in the future. That includes being skeptical of “unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts,” according to the company. The password manager will never ask its customers for an account password or a secret key.

In response, 1Password says that it has disabled the compromised GitHub account, rotated and revoked exposed internal credentials, and brought in external cybersecurity experts to advise the software maker on its response, among other measures.

Security for everybody

The world of cybersecurity moves fast – and now that cycle is speeding up even in light of AI. Security companies are leveraging artificial intelligence to detect threats at the same time that malicious actors are putting it to work cracking into accounts at scale.

1Password CTO Nancy Wang described the unique challenges and opportunities the company faces in light of widespread AI adoption in a recent interview with Fast Company. While a sea of vibe-coded apps have introduced security holes human software makers would have caught, AI can also scan massive chunks of code for vulnerabilities. “AI’s been a mixed bag, just because that work has been so gnarly and technical,” Wang said.

Aside from the millions of people who rely on 1Password, more than 200,000 businesses use the password manager to keep track of their credentials. That number includes nearly a third of the largest companies in the U.S., according to 1Password. Fast Company named the software maker to its 2025 list of Brands That Matter for its user-friendly approach to security. 

“1Password was built on the belief that security should be accessible to everyone,” 1Password CEO David Faugno said last year. “In an industry that too often leads with fear and complexity, we’ve built our foundation on trust, usability, and the human experience.”

items.title: [abcnews.com] Trump replaces national cyber director after outages disrupt US services
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

President Donald Trump replaced National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross with Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten Davies as acting director after a week of outages disrupted aviation, banking, communications and government systems. The incidents have drawn scrutiny of the administration’s response, although officials say there is no evidence of a coordinated cyberattack or a connection among the failures. A source familiar with the White House’s thinking said Trump supported Cairncross’s removal because he lacked strong cybersecurity credentials. Trump said Friday, “I didn’t think that person was good enough”. Axios reported that Chief of Staff Stephen Miller pushed for the change on similar grounds. Cairncross, a former Republican National Committee executive, said he was proud of his work in the role. Davies has held cybersecurity and technology leadership jobs at Unilever, Estée Lauder, Barclays-Africa Group, Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Siemens. Davies will serve temporarily. A permanent director must be nominated by the president and confirmed by the Senate, which Democrats are due to control in January. Cybersecurity experts say companies’ rapid efforts to patch software vulnerabilities may be behind some disruptions, as advanced AI tools make those flaws easier to find.

items.title: [cybersecuritynews.com] Swiss agency confirms four successful AI-agent hacks, including attacks on critical-infrastructure operators
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Switzerland’s National Cyber Security Centre says attackers using AI agents breached systems in four of five cases reported in the country, including attacks on three critical-infrastructure operators. The cases are part of a rise in campaigns using AI frameworks to automate reconnaissance and exploit security weaknesses. The Swiss agency has not identified the attackers, and officials reported no major outages. Italy’s incident response team says it observed campaigns in which multiple agents worked in parallel to compromise exposed systems. Canada’s cyber centre says automated tools have shortened some reconnaissance and exploitation from days or weeks to minutes. Amazon separately described agents that found and exploited an unpatched flaw on a university server in about 11 minutes. Swiss authorities advise organizations to reduce the number of internet-facing systems and install critical updates within 24 hours of release. Italy also urged operators to restrict remote-management access and monitor unusual authentication and network activity.

items.title: [krdo.com] Investigators suspect AI tool in breach of three US spy agencies
items.content_html:

Early indicators point to China, but no attacker has been publicly identified. The network processes open-source intelligence, and officials have said classified information was not compromised. The network combines publicly available material with commercially sourced datasets, social-media content and satellite imagery. Investigators have not specified what records were accessed or when the breach occurred. An ODNI official said critical capabilities and classified systems were not disrupted, and a person familiar with the incident told The Associated Press the issue had been resolved. Separately, the Treasury Department’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) disclosed that it was investigating unauthorized access to a limited subset of its systems. The agency took some systems offline as a precaution, directed banks to use its Financial Institutions Hotline for reports, and said the FBI, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) and outside forensic examiners were assessing the incident.

The agency collected more than 1,000 post-detonation samples, and laboratory results could begin arriving Friday. Testing also covers other substances that might have been released. The Army said the stockpile had become unstable and could explode accidentally as colder weather set in, making destruction in place the safest option. The EPA said it would continue monitoring while laboratories process the samples. Its pre-blast baseline included 1,591 samples, and officials said sampling covered homes, farms, parks and drinking-water sources.

Its two orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface, interior and magnetic environment, including its unusually large metal core, the origins of its magnetic field and ice in permanently shadowed craters. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival, and reaching Mercury requires careful braking against the Sun’s gravity. The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter will map the surface’s composition and study the interior; Japan’s orbiter will measure the magnetic field and the planet’s thin sodium exosphere. The spacecraft are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with science operations planned to begin in April 2027.

items.title: [tass.com] IAEA seeks ninth ceasefire to restore power at Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia plant
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), the U.N. nuclear watchdog, is negotiating with Russia and Ukraine for a ninth localized ceasefire around the Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant after it lost its connection to its last remaining external power line on Nov. 25, reportedly due to military activity. The plant has lost external power 28 times since Russia’s invasion began and is now using emergency diesel generators. All six reactors are shut down, but electricity is still needed to cool nuclear fuel and maintain essential safety systems. IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi said the plant’s reliance on one line and its location on the front line leave its offsite power connection “extremely precarious”. Russian plant operators said the line disconnected after protection devices activated and that the generators were working properly. The agency is seeking a halt to military activity around electrical infrastructure so crews can repair the 330-kilovolt Ferosplavna-1 line and reconnect the plant. The IAEA also says another key supply route, the Dniprovska 750-kilovolt line and substation, needs further work.

items.content_html:

Researchers have identified Praearcturus gigas, a scorpion known from a fossil found in the United Kingdom dating to about 415 million years ago, as a candidate for the largest known scorpion. They estimated that the animal exceeded one meter in length. A new analysis combining CT scans with traditional fossil tracings resolved decades of uncertainty over its classification. Paleontologist Richie Howard and colleagues infer that it hunted both on land and in water; terrestrial ecosystems were still developing at the time. The researchers suggest that the absence of other large predators may have enabled its large size, while later competition may have contributed to its decline.

For the past several weeks, 100 Mile Ford has been taking part in the KOT Auto Group’s eighth annual Coat Drive, the third time the dealership has participated. Carole Velne, an accountant with 100 Mile Ford, said they are looking to collect as many coats, gloves, toques and other winter accessories as possible. “For those that need a little bit more extra warmth at this time of year. We collect coats, hats, toques, mitts and scarves,” Velne said. “We pile them up into our truck and at the end of November they will all be taken out to the Cariboo Christian Life Fellowship (CCLF) church in the 108 Mile Ranch area.” As of Wednesday, Nov. 18, Velne said the Ford Ranger they’ve been storing the donations in is half full. She noted that they would welcome more donations to come in for the last few days of November. To donate, Velne said community members simply need to come by 100 Mile Ford during their regular hours of operation and drop off their donations. She noted that some have left bags of clothes by the front door when they come in to work in the morning. “We know times are tough. The economy is not booming the best right now. There’s just a lot of people out there who really can’t afford the proper warm jackets for the Cariboo weather up here,” Velne said. “Whatever little bit people can throw our way is just such a big help.” Donations will be accepted until Monday, Nov. 30. Afterwards, they’ll go to the CCLF, which will be responsible for distributing them. Velne said she is looking forward to seeing just how much winter wear they can raise. “I think whatever people have that would keep people warm would be gladly accepted.” **News** **Doerkson lays out immediate priorities, explains B.C. cabinet

items.title: [theguardian.com] Anthropic mathematician's Claude-assisted Riemann claim prompts math departments to adapt
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says the company’s Claude assistant helped him prove the Riemann hypothesis, a longstanding mathematical claim about prime-number distribution. The claimed proof remains subject to human verification. Johns Hopkins University’s mathematics department has issued guidance for Ph.D. applicants and job candidates, saying it expects transparency about AI use and will not give written work positive weight unless candidates demonstrate they understand it. Professor Yiannis Sakellaridis said the guidance was prompted by the risk that candidates could submit AI-generated proofs without learning the underlying mathematics, not by a specific applicant case. Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei rejected the idea that people should hand governance to AI, while David Krueger, founder of the nonprofit Evitable, argued that concern about losing control calls for a halt to advanced AI development. Researchers and technology leaders have debated whether the mathematical advances signal progress toward systems that exceed human capabilities.

items.title: [news.mit.edu] Older adults show weaker brain-clearing fluid waves during sleep
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

MIT researchers found that older adults had significantly weaker waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which helps clear waste from the brain during sleep, than younger adults. The researchers used brain imaging and electroencephalography to study volunteers ages 18 to 39 and 60 to 84, linking the reduced flow partly to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and diminished vascular responses. Separately, a study described in a paper shared on Reddit found that LSD-related gene-expression patterns in rats and mice ran counter to some patterns associated with human brain aging. LSD also reduced certain amyloid-beta-related changes in mouse brain-cell cultures. These are preclinical findings, not evidence that LSD prevents dementia in people.

items.title: [nation.com.pk] WHO warns rising drug resistance is eroding last-line antibiotic options
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Drug-resistant bacterial infections are increasing across regions. The World Health Organization and European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control report that European Klebsiella pneumoniae infections rose 72% from 2019 to 2025, while resistance in monitored E. coli infections also increased. Globally, one in six laboratory-confirmed common bacterial infections was resistant to antibiotics in 2023, according to the WHO. When standard antibiotics fail, clinicians may turn to carbapenems, but resistance to these last-line drugs is also rising. In the Americas, carbapenem resistance in Klebsiella pneumoniae increased from about 15% in 2015 to 26% in 2024; median resistance in Acinetobacter baumannii was 77% across the seven reporting countries. Health authorities are calling for stronger infection prevention, laboratory diagnosis and surveillance; the Pan American Health Organization’s 2027–2031 action plan was approved in September.

items.title: [al-monitor.com] Saudi strikes on Hodeidah port threaten Yemen's key aid route
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

The Saudi-led coalition struck Yemen’s Red Sea port of Hodeidah on Friday after warning civilians to leave, saying it targeted facilities used to smuggle weapons and ballistic missiles. Hodeidah is a main entry point for food and other supplies to Houthi-held northern Yemen. The United Nations warned that escalation could threaten aid routes relied on by millions. Yemen’s information minister said the port remained fully operational and goods would continue to flow. The coalition also reported strikes against Houthi military capabilities in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz. In southern Saudi Arabia, it said air defenses intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Jazan, with debris falling near the Shuqaiq area. The Houthis claimed attacks on a power station there and Jazan port. Air India and Air India Express suspended flights to and from Jeddah until Nov. 24, while flights to Riyadh and Dammam remained suspended until Nov. 30, the Indian embassy in Riyadh said.
